proposal.root_problem: Customers experience unresolved, indefinite waiting for refund outcomes because a subset of refunds fail to complete at the payment-data-validation step, surfacing as status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT in payment-db (E-01), not because support agents are slow or a self-service channel is missing (ticket-db shows median 2.0h response vs a 24h SLA across 900 tickets, E-02). The invalid/malformed IBAN data blocks refund completion, so there is no final outcome for customers to be told about, regardless of channel or response speed.
proposal.requested_solution: Build a chatbot so customers get instant self-service answers about refund status (initial request, CL-01/CL-02).
symptoms: Customers report waiting indefinitely for answers about refund status (SH-SUP, E-03/CL-01/CL-02).
All 5 sampled payment-db refund_failures records show status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT, i.e., the refunds never completed (E-01).
Support ticket response times are well within SLA (median 2.0h vs 24h SLA, 900 tickets), so the complaint is not explained by agent response delay (E-02).
causal_chain: Upstream data capture produces invalid/malformed IBAN values for some refund records (interpretation of E-01).
payment-db rejects these refund transactions, recording status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT (E-01).
The refund never completes, leaving no resolved outcome for the customer (E-01).
Agents nonetheless respond to related tickets well within SLA (median 2.0h vs 24h, 900 tickets, E-02), so slow agent response is not the cause.
Customers continue to perceive an unresolved wait because the refund itself is stuck, which the support lead (SH-SUP) misattributes to a missing self-service answer channel (E-03).

The other remedies (SR-R2/R3/R4) and bank-api:settlement_status are excluded: they are not in release_scope (they sit in unfinished_scope / are blocked by OPEN VOBs VOB-U-IBAN-FAILURE-POPULATION-SCOP and VOB-U-TICKET-PAYMENT-SYNC-GAP), and bank-api:settlement_status already produced a NOT_TRANSIENT ACCESS_DENIED HOLD (recent_events seq 48) with no fallback path, so re-querying it would not add value. The already-executed catalog refs (interview:SH-SUP, payment-db:refund_failures, ticket-db:response_times, per already_executed) are not repeated.

proposal.summary: The initial request (SH-SUP, CL-01/CL-02) asked for a chatbot so customers stop waiting for refund-status answers, but investigation (PD-1) found the real root problem is that a subset of refunds fail to complete at the payment-data-validation step (status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT), not slow support response. The release delivers only the upstream fix for that root cause — an IBAN-format validation check at refund data capture (add_iban_validation_check:P-REF) — under decision RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, while diagnosis/cleanup of existing failed refunds and the ticket-payment sync question remain open and out of this release's scope.
key_points: Problem as defined (PD-1): customers experience indefinite waiting because some refunds never complete due to invalid/malformed IBAN data at the validation step (E-01: all 5 sampled payment-db refund_failures records show status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT), not because support is slow or a self-service channel is missing (E-02: ticket-db median response 2.0h vs 24h SLA across 900 tickets).

How it was established: the original framing (CL-01, CL-02, restated non-authoritatively by SH-SUP in E-03) that a chatbot/self-service channel is needed was tested against hypotheses; H-NO-SELF-SERVICE-CHANNEL, H-AGENT-CAPACITY-BACKLOG and H-SLOW-REFUND-PROCESSING were REJECTED (contradicted by E-01/E-02), while H-REFUND-IBAN-VALIDATION-FAILU was SUPPORTED by E-01 and E-02.

What was released: the solution design's release_scope (SD-1) is limited to add_iban_validation_check on process P-REF (work item W-WI-1-IBAN-VALIDATION), which adds an IBAN-format check at refund data capture so malformed IBANs are rejected before entering payment-db; this is also the minimum_useful_scope.

Why this is the release decision: the DEFINE gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS with critical unknowns deferred to verification obligations (VOB-U-IBAN-FAILURE-POPULATION-SCOP, VOB-U-TICKET-PAYMENT-SYNC-GAP, VOB-R-3), all still OPEN; their blocking_scope (diagnose_iban_failure_scope, correct_iban_data, resolve_refund, monitor_response_sla) falls outside the released scope, so the release proceeds with known limitations rather than being held.
The tool bank-api is DEGRADED, which affects resolve_refund:DA-PAY (per U-BANK-API-RELEVANCE/VOB-R-3) and is one reason correction of existing failed refunds was not released this round.

A separate candidate hypothesis, H-TICKET-PAYMENT-DISCONNECT (ticket-db/payment-db desynchronization), remains unresolved (status CANDIDATE) and is tied to the still-open VOB-U-TICKET-PAYMENT-SYNC-GAP.
limitations_explained: The true prevalence of IBAN-format failures beyond the 5 sampled records (E-01) is not established; VOB-U-IBAN-FAILURE-POPULATION-SCOP is still OPEN, so confidence in the overall scope of the failure pattern is limited.

The released validation check only prevents future malformed-IBAN refunds; it does not correct or resolve the existing FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT refunds identified in E-01, which remain blocked on the DEGRADED bank-api (ACCESS_DENIED) and the open VOB-U-IBAN-FAILURE-POPULATION-SCOP.

Success criterion SC-NO-FAILED-IBAN-REMAINING is not met this round: the work to correct malformed IBAN data and resolve the affected refunds (correct_iban_data:DA-PAY, resolve_refund:DA-PAY) is explicitly listed as unfinished.

Whether ticket-db and payment-db are desynchronized, which could independently prevent agents from seeing current refund status, is unverified (VOB-U-TICKET-PAYMENT-SYNC-GAP OPEN); as a result, monitor_response_sla:DA-TCK is not part of this release.
VOB-R-3 (whether the DEGRADED bank-api issue interferes with resolving IBAN-failed refunds) remains OPEN and its blocking_scope (correct_iban_data, resolve_refund) is excluded from this release.

The underlying assumption that the 5-record sample is representative of a broader pattern (A-SAMPLE-REPRESENTATIVE) and that IBAN errors originate upstream rather than from a payment-db validation defect (A-UPSTREAM-CAPTURE-CAUSE) are both unverified assumptions, not confirmed facts.
